scenes.title: Recall
scenes.sub: Bee remembers what you heard. Recall makes sure you do.

beats.name: Problem
beats.vo: Bee hears everything I learn: lectures, study sessions, podcasts. It can summarize them and remember them for me. But in an interview, I'm the one who has to know it.

beats.name: Loop
beats.vo: Practicing recall is one of the best-tested ways to learn. Recall turns what Bee heard into quizzes on my wrist that I answer out loud. Bee's transcript is the answer sheet.

beats.name: How it works
beats.vo: When a learning session ends, Recall pulls the transcript through the Bee CLI and skips anything casual or personal. Claude Haiku on Amazon Bedrock writes the questions, each tied to the moment I heard it. When I'm free, I say so, or tick a todo. Each question goes out as a Bee todo with an alarm. Recall reads Bee's live transcript while I'm talking, grades me against a rubric, and sends feedback the same way. Spaced repetition decides when I see it again.

beats.name: Why waits
beats.vo: My first version quizzed me at random times. Six prompts, four missed: driving, asleep, or the alert hit my phone. So Recall waits for you. It nudges after a lecture and in your active hours, holds off while Bee hears you talking, and a missed question never counts against you.
